D001-D008_h001.question_both:
Lately, I’ve just been… off. It’s hard to pin down exactly when it started—maybe a few weeks ago, maybe longer. I’m a crypto trader, so I’m used to fast-paced days, but now it feels like my brain won’t slow down even when the market’s closed. I’ll sit down to analyze a chart or balance my portfolio, but halfway through, I’ll get sidetracked by an unrelated thought—a meme I saw, a news headline, even the sound of traffic outside. Organizing my trades or sticking to a schedule? Forget it. I keep promising myself I’ll set up a system, but I never follow through.

I’m also talking way more than usual—my friends have noticed. I’ll call them and just go on for ages, jumping from one idea to another. Sometimes I don’t even remember what we talked about. I feel like I’m wired—can’t sit still, like I need to be doing ten things at once. I’ll start coding a bot, then switch to researching altcoins, then decide I need to redesign my whole workspace. Nothing gets finished.

I’ve had intense periods before, but this time, I’m not sure if it’s just me being me… or something more. It hasn’t *totally* derailed things, but it’s starting to worry me.
D001-D008_h001.question_a:
I’ve always struggled with focus and restlessness, even as a kid. Teachers used to say I had potential but couldn’t stick with one thing. I remember homework piling up because I didn’t know where to start—same with chores or planning my day. That’s still me now, honestly. At work, tracking different crypto markets pulls my attention in ten directions. I’ll start analyzing BTC trends, then jump to altcoins, then check news—before I know it, I’ve lost the thread entirely.

I’m always moving—fidgeting, pacing, talking. My friends say I monologue. I don’t mean to, but thoughts spill out fast, and I hate silences. It’s like I’m wired too tight. This has been non-stop since I was *maybe* eight or nine. I’ve always been like this.

About a year ago, though, I had this intense burst of energy—slept three hours a night, spent recklessly, felt invincible. It only lasted a few days. But even before that, and long after, the distraction and constant motion were still there. The “high” came and went, but the rest never did. It’s not the mania driving it—it’s *always* been there, under everything.
D001-D008_h001.question_b:
I’ve been struggling a lot lately—work’s been wild, but honestly, even when the market’s calm, my mind won’t shut off. I’ll start analyzing charts, then jump to news, then start texting five different people at once about trades I haven’t even confirmed. It’s like I can’t organize my thoughts—everything’s happening at once. I know I’m talking nonstop; my friends have called me out, saying I don’t give them space to respond.

There was this one stretch a few weeks ago—didn’t sleep for three nights, felt amazing, like I finally cracked the code. I made wild trades, big moves, felt like I *knew* what the market would do. That’s when all the distraction and restlessness got worse—couldn’t stick to one idea, kept starting new spreadsheets, sending rapid messages, just *moving*. But when that wave crashed, I crashed too—couldn’t get out of bed, didn’t want to check anything.

I’ve always had some focus issues, sure, but this hyper, talkative, scattered version of me? It only shows up during these intense, up periods—those manic highs. Outside of them, I’m not like that.

    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)

I’ll start a project with so much energy, sketching, modeling, talking through ideas nonstop to anyone who’ll listen—my coworkers probably think I never pause—but then I’ll lose track of details, miss revisions, or get pulled off task by a random thought or noise. I’m always *doing*, like I can’t sit still. My mind races, and I end up talking over people without realizing it.  

There have been times—especially last year—when I felt this intense burst of confidence, barely slept, and took on three projects at once. I thought I was unstoppable. But when that faded, the disorganization and distractibility didn’t. They were there before, during, and after. It’s not that my mood drives the chaos—it’s the other way around. The restlessness and inattention? They’ve been with me since childhood, steady as breathing, no matter how I feel emotionally.

People said I seemed “wound too tight,” like I was vibrating.

I’d bounce around during class, couldn’t sit still even when I tried, and teachers always said I was disorganized or disruptive. Back then, I just thought I was wired differently. Now, as a fitness trainer, people see me as energetic, which helps with clients, but behind the scenes, I’m a mess. I forget to follow up on emails, lose my gym bag, miss appointments—even with clients I like. Planning my day feels overwhelming; I start five things at once and finish none.  

The last few months have been worse. I had this intense burst of energy—barely sleeping, talking fast, taking on too many shifts—but that’s new. Before that, the forgetfulness and restlessness were always there, even when I wasn’t feeling that "high." That crash after? That’s new too. But the not listening, the losing stuff, the needing to be constantly moving—that never goes away, whether I’m up, down, or in between. It’s like background noise, always on.
D001-D008_h013.question_b:
I’ve been feeling… off the charts lately—like I’ve got this unstoppable energy. As a fitness trainer, I’m used to being on the move, but this is different. For the past three weeks, I barely sleep—like two hours a night—and I’m still wide awake, buzzing. I’ve been planning five new workout programs, revamping my entire schedule, even calling clients at 3 a.m. to pitch ideas. I know it’s too much, but I can’t slow down.

The thing is, I keep losing my phone, missing appointments I swore I’d make—total chaos trying to run my own business. I’ll start organizing client files, then jump up and start redesigning the gym layout. I can’t sit still, even during a stretch session. It’s like my body won’t listen. Waiting my turn in line? Forget it. I’ll just cut ahead without thinking.

But here’s the thing—this never happened before this burst of energy hit. All these focus problems, the restlessness—it didn’t exist last month, or the year before. It just exploded when this manic high started. I’ve never felt like this in my life, and honestly, it’s starting to scare me.

D001-D008_h022.question_both:
I’ve been struggling a lot lately, especially with my coursework. I’ll sit down to write a paper or study, and I start okay, but then I just lose focus—little things distract me, like my phone buzzing or even the clock ticking. I catch myself rereading the same paragraph over and over, and then I realize I’ve made the same formatting mistake three times. It’s frustrating, because I know I’m smart enough, but I can’t seem to finish what I start. I’ve missed a few deadlines, not because I forgot, but because I never got to the final steps, even when I meant to.

At the same time, I feel… restless. Like I can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted. I’m always moving—pacing while reading, clicking pens, getting up to do something else mid-task. My friends say I interrupt them a lot, and I see it now—I’ll jump into a conversation before they’re done, not to be rude, but because the thought feels urgent, like if I don’t say it now, I’ll lose it.

There have been periods where I felt unusually energized, like I needed less sleep but wasn’t tired—maybe lasting a few days—where I’d take on too many projects at once. But it never lasted long enough to feel like a full episode, and the focus problems were there even when I wasn’t feeling that way.
D001-D008_h022.question_a:
I’ve struggled with focusing since I was a kid—like, elementary school age. I’d rush through assignments and skip steps, even when I wanted to do well. Teachers said I was smart but careless. That never really went away. Now in grad school, I’ll start reading a paper and end up distracted by my phone or just zoning out, and then miss key details on exams. I often don’t finish what I start, whether it’s a research draft or even just replying to emails.

I’m always moving—fidgeting, pacing, feeling restless like I can’t sit still. My friends joke that I’m “wired,” and I’ll jump into group conversations without waiting, sometimes finishing people’s sentences. It’s embarrassing, but I can’t help it.

Last semester, I had a period where I barely slept but was hyper-focused, almost racing—my advisor thought I might be manic. But here’s the thing: the inattention and feeling “on the go”? That’s been with me since *before* I was 12. The racing thoughts came and went, but the focus and impulsivity—they’ve never left.

I’ll start reading and then realize I’ve made no sense of it, even though my mind’s racing. It’s not that I’m not trying. I sit down to work, but I keep jumping up, pacing, checking emails 10 times, starting new projects. I’ve interrupted professors during office hours, jumped into group discussions without waiting my turn. It’s like I can’t hit pause.

But here’s the thing—before this, I was never like this. I got all As in undergrad. I was organized, focused. These attention problems, the constant movement, the impulsiveness—they didn’t exist before this intense period where I barely slept, felt invincible. My advisor said I was “too much.” Now I’m crashing, but the trouble following through, the mistakes… they started with that high, and they’ve stuck.

Lately, I find myself walking into the barn and forgetting why I went there, or missing spots when I’m checking the fences. I used to take pride in being thorough, but now I’ll start a task—like fixing a gate—and get halfway through, then realize I’ve wandered off to do something else. My wife mentioned I left the tractor running the other day while I went inside to argue about the weather with no real reason. That wasn’t like me.

I’ve been restless, too. Can’t sit still during supper, always feel like I need to be moving—even when there’s no hurry. My wife says I’ve been cutting her off mid-sentence, jumping into things without waiting. I don’t mean to. It’s like my body’s ahead of my thoughts.

There are times I feel wired, like I could work through the night, though I don’t actually finish what I start. But then other days, I’m flat. Not real up, not real down. Just… scattered. I can’t tell if it’s stress, getting older, or something more.

Truth is, I’ve felt like my mind’s always been racing, like I’m driven by some inner motor. I can’t sit still, even at dinner.

Now, there are times I feel supercharged—like I don’t need sleep, full of big ideas—where I talk fast and take risks, like almost buying a tractor I can’t afford. But those high periods come and go. The rest of the time, the inattention and restlessness? They’ve been with me since I was a kid—long before these mood spikes ever started. Since last week, the energy just crashed. I’m exhausted now, barely want to go outside. But those restless, scattered weeks—they were unlike anything before. And truth is, nothing like this ever happened when I was younger. It just came on fast with this… high.
